blocks.html: The base shiny rate is 1/4096. When the Shiny Charm is held, this increases to 1/100. The shiny charm is given by Professor Hawthorne when assassing your Pokedex in person, if 75%+ of the dex is filled.
The Masuda breeding method and chain fishing are in the game. Masuda breeding will be challenging because there are limited in game trades and no external trades.
If you attempt to run from a shiny, you will be asked to confirm so you don’t accidentally mispress. If the All Shinies game modifier is on, this confirmation will not happen.

blocks.html: Additionally, more pokemon can use Terrain Pulse now, to make its TM reward more useful.
Fossil resurrection is not present in the game. They are instead found in the wild like normal Pokemon.
The beast ball has a 0.1x rate on all non-Ultra Beast Pokemon. Necrozma and its forms are considered Ultra Beasts for PokeBall checks.

Prior to choosing an action (attacking, switching, etc.), type icons will pop up in battle for both you and your opponent(s). While the game will always show the effectiveness of moves when choosing to attack, this can be helpful when deciding what to switch to.
The Freeze status has been replaced with Frostbite. When afflicted, Pokemon lose 1/16th of their HP each turn and their special attack is halved. It’s functionally special-burn.
When starting an encounter in dark grass (right in screenshot), there is a 50% chance to trigger a wild double battle. Pokemon cannot be caught unless the other found Pokemon has fainted.

As the player’s Pokedex entries fill up with caught Pokemon, the player is increasingly likely to perform a Critical Capture. When this happens, the ball shakes in midair and only has to shake once for a capture to be performed. The chance of this occurring is driven by the Pokedex’s completion rate, as well as the catch rate of the Pokemon (modified based on their hp, status, and the ball being used).
Holding the Catching Charm (given by an NPC in Heleo City’s Pokemon Center after successfully completing 5 critical captures) doubles the likelihood of triggering a critical capture.

Important trainers like gym leaders and rivals will trigger mugshots before their battles, for dramatic effect:
When battling these trainers, they will also slide in during the battle to remark on the following events:

items: Their first Pokemon faints
Their last Pokemon is sent in
Their last Pokemon is at low HP

blocks.html: Furthermore, Gym Leaders’ battle music will change when they send out their last Pokemon, leading to a thrilling finale to the fight!
During certain points in the story, the player will team up with another trainer to battle for a bit. The player brings the first 3 Pokemon in their party, and the other trainer does the same.

rows: Rival or Alistair, player can swap at will

blocks.html: When travelling with another trainer during the Route 11 South Team Pluto event, the player will be healed after each battle.

All Pokemon in the Pokedex have mega stones, which can either be found in the overworld or through exploration. Mega Stones can be collected any time, but can only be used after Team Pluto is thwarted on Route 11.
See Locations > Mega Stones for where Mega Stones can be found. As a reminder, mega Pokemon availability depends on the mode you are playing (Standard or Divergent) as of v1.3.

All official mega Pokemon are unchanged (re: their stats, types, and abilities), while Pokemon with Gigantamax forms have had those forms converted into Megas, complete with stat, ability, and type changes that I felt were reflective of their new forms.

blocks.html: PokeChips are a new currency introduced in Pokemon Amethyst, which are used at various vendors such as Move Tutors. They are randomly received after wild battles with the following criteria:

rows: Battle started with Sweet Scent or Honey

blocks.html: For example, if you have the PokeChip Charm and used Sweet Scent to start the battle, your chance of finding a PokeChip is 60%. In double wild battles, each Pokemon has a chance to drop a PokeChip.

Game Modifiers allow the player to tweak the way the game works, and can be freely toggled off and on at the PC in the player’s room. Each can be unlocked by completing postgame criteria (each of which is mentioned by the modifier itself) or with a code (to allow it to be used in new games).

The codes are provided here, which can be copy-pasted to a text editor to reveal. While I recommend playing Pokemon Amethyst for the first time without modifiers to get the intended experience, it’s ultimately your decision and you can choose what’s fun for you!

rows:
Allows players to randomize all Pokemon encountered in the game. The player may choose to randomize with Pokemon found in Kulure or all from gens 1-8.
This is a 1:1 replacement based on a unique seed on the save. If Rattata is replaced by Jirachi, all Rattata will become Jirachis.
Note: this is fully supported as of v1.4. Some items are present in game data but otherwise inaccessible (ex. DNA Splicers), in case you want to hack them in.

All battles use the Inverse battle ruleset, where type effectiveness is reversed.
This is not disabled by the Heleo City Trainer House.

All battles use the Camomon battle ruleset, where a Pokemon’s type is dedicated by the types of its first two moves.
This is not disabled by the Emraldin Quay Trainer House.
All battles (whenever possible) are double battles. This requires both trainers to have 2+ healthy Pokemon.

The player can attempt to catch any trainer’s Pokemon. The battle will end immediately after.
The Pokemon’s OT and IVs are dependent on the trainer and their trainer class, respectively.
Wild Pokemon always scale to the highest level in the player’s party.

Trainer Pokemons’ levels are always scaled to the highest level in the player’s party.
Some trainers already do this in the game. If this modifier is active, the scaling is not disabled after those battles.
All Pokemon are generated with their hidden abilities, if they have one.
The move reminder in Daimyn City will teach level up moves regardless of the Pokemon’s current level.
If a held item is consumed or otherwise lost in battle, it is restored afterward.
The player can see all Pokemon on a route in the DexNav interface, without the need to have seen it already.
All battles start with a chosen weather. This is not overridden by overworld locations but can be by a Pokemon’s ability or move.
All battles start with a chosen terrain. This is not overridden by overworld locations but can be by a Pokemon’s ability or move.
All Pokemon are generated with max friendship.
All wild Pokemon have perfect IVs once caught. Introduced in v1.4
The EV/IV Viewer can be accessed from a Pokemon’s Stats Screen. Introduced in v1.3.
Mega Evolution can be used multiple times per battle. Introduced in v1.4
Adds the ability to flip between Standard and Divergent Species modes in the Options menu. Introduced in v1.3.

blocks.html: As of v1.4.3 you may enter the Konami Code while in the player’s room to unlock all remaining game modifiers. This is provided to make challenge runners’ lives a bit easier.
Apricorn balls can be bought in Laplaz Town for 2 PokeChips, once per day. All apricorn balls are available (Fast Ball, Level Ball, Lure Ball, Heavy Ball, Love Ball, Friend Ball, and Moon Ball).
Additionally, a traveller in Daimyn City’s Pokemon Center will sell a random special ball once per day. This can be a Safari Ball, Sport Ball, Park Ball, or Dream Ball.

Players can change the Poke Ball a Pokemon is in in Bruccie Village. This will cost 2 PokeChips and can be used for any ball except for Dynamax (which are not available in game; this would come from cheats) and Cherish balls.
The original ball is lost until the worker becomes skilled after performing 5 jobs, after which you’ll receive the original ball back.

In Tsarvosa City, the player can crush excess PokeChips to craft items from. This is a great way to convert unneeded chips into useful items, especially in the postgame when tutoring becomes less impactful.

A Pokemon’s friendship is represented by a heart in their summary screen, which fills as affection grows. Friendship can grow by walking, staying in the daycare, using items on the Pokemon, or by using the Pokemon Groomer’s services in Heleo City.
Pokemon with 220 (or more) out of 255 friendship points will gain 1.2x EXP in battle.
The Kulure region’s gyms focus on battle mechanics instead of type specialty.

The Gym Trainees, found in a house in Tsarvosa City, fill the conventional type-focused gap left by gyms with a trainee for each type. When entering the house, 3-5 of the available 18 types are chosen at random. Saving is disabled here, due to how trainees are loaded into the map.
When a trainee is defeated, they will give the player items related to their type specialty:

items: The type-raising item (ex. Charcoal, Mystic Water, etc.)
The type-specific gem (ex. Fire Gem, Water Gem, etc.)
The super-effective damage reducing berry (ex. Occa Berry, Passho Berry, etc.)

blocks.html: Afterward, they will offer to teach any Pokemon of their specialty type 1 of 3 moves, chosen at random. See Move Tutors’ Special section for more details.

After clearing the postgame Ultra Episode, they will also give the player their respective Z-Crystal, if the player beats them with a team containing only their specialty type (dual-types are permitted).

In v1.4, species-specific Z-Crystals can be purchased at the Battle Frontier. Some Z-Crystals are unavailable due to their species not being found through normal play (ex. Mew); their item data is present in the game and fully tested in case you want to hack the item in yourself.
The Move Relearner and Deleter are both found in Daimyn City, north of the Interdimensional Research Facility. Their services include:

rows: Learn an egg move (even if not learned previously)

blocks.html: EVs
EVs are earned in battles as usual, but can be manipulated in the following ways:

items: Reducing them with berries bought at Daimyn City Mall and Tsarvosa City (-10 per)
Vitamins bought at Daimyn City Mall and Tsarvosa City Stats Dojo (+10 per)
Battling disciples at the Tsarvosa City Stats Dojo

blocks.html: The disciples are key to efficient EV training. There is a disciple for each stat, each of which can be battled repeatedly to earn EVs. Like IVs, the player can invest in these disciples to unlock higher tier teams with higher EV yields.

Furthermore, the player can buy and level up Power Items from the stats dojo which give EVs per Pokemon defeated. Note that you must invest in the dojo’s shops twice ($70,000 total) to unlock power items.

Pokerus can be caught anywhere in the game with the usual rate (3 in 65,536). In Mimmett Jungle, this rate is increased to 6x it’s usual rate(to 18 in 65,536). Pokemon with Pokerus earn double EVs and can spread it to other Pokemon as usual.

When combining these factors, you can level up EVs extremely quickly. Even when factoring out pokerus, the rates in a single trainee fight can become:

(3 per pokemon + 24 from max level power item) * 3 pokemon = 81 EVs per battle
With a per-stat cap of 252, it only takes 3.5 battles to max a stat.
Abilities
A Pokemon’s ability can be changed with Ability Capsules and Ability Patches. Both items can be created by crushing PokeChips in Tsarvosa City.

items: Ability Capsule: Change from Hidden -> Standard, or Standard -> Standard
Ability Patch: Standard -> Hidden, or Hidden -> Standard

blocks.html: Greninja and Battle Bond
Greninja cannot have its ability changed to Battle Bond in this way! It must be done by talking to Selene in the postgame on route 19 and showing her a Greninja with max friendship.
Natures
A pokemon’s stat color will change in the summary, depending on whether it is affected by their nature or not:

items: Black: no change
Blue: -10%

blocks.html: A Pokemon’s nature can be changed with Clancy in Uteya Village for 10 PokeChips.

The Daycare on Route 5 works like most Pokemon games, where you can leave up to 2 Pokemon and have a chance for an egg to be laid. There’s a nice long road spanning from Ferrox Village through Routes 5 and 6 without interruption to support egg runs.

blocks.html: These can be changed at any time without penalty; there is no reward or incentive to keep difficulty or level cap settings as-is if it isn’t enjoyable for you!

Overworld and battle speed are constrained by the hardware you are playing on - emulators tend to do fine but physical devices may struggle at 3x and 4x. These features are provided for convenience and cannot be optimized much further.
Battle speedup plays music and cries at full speed; a cry must complete before the battle continues. Text speeds up too, and can be fine tuned by adjusting the global text speed setting.

Overworld speed affects just the player and followers. It is temporarily disabled whenever precision is required: DexNav scans and certain gym puzzles. NOTE: Depending on how quickly you move through map transitions, you may briefly see graphical glitches. That is a byproduct of this feature.

Starting in v1.3, players who have become champion can donate unneeded Pokemon to a researcher outside of Tsarvosa City’s Pokemon Center. The player receives PokeChips based on the quality of their donation, with the following rules in place:
Base   = round( √(Level × BST) ÷ 50 )        (minimum 1)
Level  : +1 per 10 levels starting at 60      (+1 at 60, +2 at 70 … +5 at 100)
IVs    : +1 if total IVs ≥ 140, −1 if ≤ 46
EVs    : +1 if total EVs ≥ 400
Shiny  : ×2 (applied last)
Some example payouts are:

rows: Above, with 140+ Ivs, and also shiny

blocks.html: The EXP Share is given to the player to the east of Daimyn City, and works like the EXP Share from gen 6 and onward (i.e. it splits EXP to all participating pokemon). It can be toggled off and on from the Key Items pocket.
Note: The game is balanced around not using the Exp Share.
DexNav

The DexNav allows you to find specific Pokemon in the environment. It is used via the Tools menu (Start -> Right). When scanning for a Pokemon, you’ll see patches of grass shake, bubbles form, or dust clouds get kicked up. Walking toward one will trigger a battle against that Pokemon.
When encountering a Pokemon in water or caves, it has a chance to jump to another tile when approached (40% for first time, 20% for second).
By defeating Pokemon found via the dexnav, you can increase its search level and enhance the Pokemon you find with it. These levels are:
As well, as the search level increases, the odds of finding Pokemon with perfect IVs increases. Each star level represents one stat at 31.
The DexNav UI will show a badge when all Pokemon on that route are caught. This is purely cosmetic outside of an optional rival event.

Increasing your chain to different thresholds increases the likelihood of getting a shiny. The game makes additional checks against the 1/4196 (base odds) or 1/100 (Shiny Charm odds) depending on your chain. Once you hit a chain of 100, the count no longer increases to indicate you are at maximum odds.
Prior to version 1.4, the increased shiny odds occurred only at chain 50 & 100. As of 1.4, it applies to every chain level afterward.

Each Pokemon with Pickup has a 10% chance to find an item after battle. For convenience, these items are sent directly to the bag. You have a 98% chance to find an item from the Common Pool and a 2% chance from the Rare Pool.

blocks.html: Pokemon swarms are events where a Pokemon normally found on a route may be replaced by a regional variant. When on one of these routes, you have a 50% chance to encounter the swarming Pokemon. The swarming species changes each day and can be revealed by talking to the Swarm Swami in Heleo City.
When catching a swarming Pokemon, its Kulure-native equivalent is registered as caught. For example, catching Rattata will mark Rattata-A as caught.

If the player shows a regional variant or its evolutions to the Swami’s assistant, they will receive a bottlecap (first time only). This only applies to swarm-based evolutions (ex. Goomy offers no reward, but Hisuian Sliggoo and Goodra do). After showing all, they will receive a gold bottlecap.
The following variants cannot be found:

items: Deviating evolutions (eg. Purrzerker)
Kantonian birds

blocks.html: Because of the Slowpoke family, Galaric Cuffs and Wreaths can be bought in Emraldin Quay. Black Augurites can also be bought there in divergent mode, for Kleavor evolutions.
Roaming Pokemon appear on the Town Map to make them easier to track. Roamers change locations whenever the player enters/exits buildings, changes named locations, or flies.
All roamers and other legendaries are created with 3 perfect IVs. You have a 25% chance of triggering a roamer fight while on their route. Roamers cannot leave the islands they spawn on.
If a roamer or legendary has fainted, it will reappear the next time the player enters the Hall of Fame.
This game features the popular DNS system by utilizing the Real-Type Clock (RTC) system. The following time ranges apply:

items: Morning: 4AM - 8AM
Day: 8AM - 5PM
Evening: 5PM - 8PM
Night: 8PM - 4AM

blocks.html: Functionally, Morning/Day and Evening/Night are the same when it comes to things like wild encounters and evolutions, with one minor difference: Rockruff can only evolve into Lycanroc Dusk in the Evening timeframe.

The Pokedex’s catch map will also update to reflect the current time. For example, checking Varisi Forest for Hoothoot during the day will result in it not being found, but at night it will appear on the catch map. Many trainers will also hint at these kinds of encounters.
In certain environments, the DNS is flipped so night occurs during the day.
Battle backgrounds are provided for all encounters. These also change based on the time of day, in outdoor maps!
In many maps, you may talk to nurses to heal your party without needing to return to a Pokemon Center. Just be careful - they may want to battle first!
In some locations, you may encounter static Pokemon posing as traps!

rows: Sandygast and Palossand pretend to be sandcastles
Foongus and Amoonguss pretend to be Pokeballs (they appear slightly smaller)
Stunfisk waits to snare unsuspecting trainers (they appear as tiny pokeball icons surrounded by teeth)

blocks.html: Some maps have variable weather or permanent terrain set in battle. These are overridden by any active game modifiers.

blocks.html: Oftentimes, the game will present you with multiple paths through a route when heading to your destination. In some cases, you may even have the option of taking completely separate routes!

Notably, the game opens up after gym 2, then funnels back in before you can challenge gym 6. This means you can tackle exploration and gyms 3-5 in any order you choose. Earlier gym leaders will receive buffed teams if they are battled out of order, but later gym leaders will always have the same team.  In practice, this means Casey has 1 team while Raine has 3, depending on whether she’s fought 3rd, 4th or 5th.

The Daimyn City restaurant lets you prepare meals that strengthen the entire party for a limited number of battles. You can invest money and PokeChips into the shop to increase the meals available and their durations. The effects of meals do not stack.

In v1.3, players can choose to play the game with the Standard Pokemon list or the Divergent Pokemon list. Standard is recommended for a first playthrough, with Divergent mode offered for players looking for a fresh experience. Generally speaking, Divergent mode is easier due to having less flexibility when designing boss trainer teams.

When Divergent mode is enabled, the Pokedex updates to replace all Pokemon from entries 1-300 with a new, hand-curated set (excluding Rotom, Ditto, Jirachi, and Victini). This is not a 1:1 swap; all wild Pokemon, trainer teams, legendaries, shop stock, and trades are replaced with fresh lists of Pokemon that make sense for the location and trainer theme. The only thing that does not change are gift Pokemon given to the player.
New Game Modifier

The modes were implemented as separate options to not dilute Pokemon selection in either mode, while still providing a way for players to use their favorites and experience a fresh take on the game. While Divergent mode is intended to be set-and-forget, I do understand the appeal of being able to play with your favorites. A new Game Modifier is added that allows the player to swap between modes via the Options menu, unlocked when completing the game in Divergent mode.

When swapping, the following occurs:

items: Wild Pokemon and trainers update automatically
The Pokedex, DexNav, and PokeDex Assessment all update to reflect the current mode
This means you can aim for dex completion in both modes
The Pokedex’s Habitat list includes all caught Pokemon from the alternate mode, presented as #000 (This is a technical limitation, but it is nice to see everything in one place anyways)
Shops refresh their inventory for mode-specific items (Mega Stones and evolution items in Tsarvosa City)
Legendary Pokemon are refreshed
Roaming legendaries swap automatically. For roamers that have fainted, the player must enter the Hall of Fame to get them to roam again
Certain mode-specific overworld items are refreshed
Stick / Sachet on Route 7
Blue Orb / Reveal Glass in Uteyan Ruins
Red Orb / Prison Bottle in Uteyan Ruins
Rusted Data / Genesect Drives in Daimyn City Factory
All Mega Stones (also serves as a way to restore lost mega stones)
After clearing the Carnelidge Volcano story sequence, the player also receives the Houndoominite / Tyranitarite when swapping, if they aren’t in the bag

The Battle Frontier is introduced in v1.4 and becomes accessible to players after becoming the champion, by visiting the Tsarvosa City Pier. After arriving, they are free to fly to/from the frontier at any time. This facility features both Singles and Doubles battles at 8 different facilities, each with its own spin on battling. The player can customize the battle background and music used when battling at any facility.

The player can also arrive at the Frontier if they interact with the dresser in their bedroom prior to receiving their starter. This is a one-way trip and is meant to be used for demoing purposes, or if you are just interested in enjoying tough battles. When taking this route, the player is given 30 Singles-ready and Doubles-ready Pokemon in their PC box.
Shared Ruleset
The frontier is made up of 8 different facilities described in greater detail below, but all share the same rules:

items: Pokemon and movesets from other regions may appear
Pokemon scale to level 50 and do not gain exp
Consumed held items are returned after battle
Difficulty settings don’t apply; all opponents are EV and IV trained
Resetting once a battle has begun results in a forfeit
Game Modifiers and Meal Effects are temporarily disabled while in a frontier battle

A streak may be paused at any time and resumed later. You may bring a different team when resuming, with the exception of the Battle Factory which restores the party you had. Both Singles and Doubles can be paused at the same time.

blocks.html: Rewards
Players earn PokeChips for each win, with growing streaks giving additional chips. When beating an Ace or Brain at streak 20 and 50 respectively, 20 and 50 chips are given instead:
As the player hits max streak milestones, they earn stars on their Battle Record:

items: Bronze star: 20
Silver star: 50
Gold star: 100

blocks.html: When a streak of 50+ has been reached at any facility, a star is added to the player’s Trainer Card. All other rewards (held items, Z-Crystals, tutor moves, etc.) can be received without participating in a single Battle Frontier battle, if the player wishes.
Opponent Teambuilding

Opponents are randomly built from a pool of 2,033 different builds. Each species can only appear once (prior to streak 31) and typically has 4-6 spreads. This means there are billions of unique team combinations; you’ll almost never face the same twice. The opponent’s team is generated just before a battle occurs and factors your current team into its teambuilding process. The pool for these is genuinely massive.
Aces and Brains have smaller teambuilding pools with species specific to that trainer. For example, your rival brings Pokemon he acquires in the standard and divergent modes.
Opponent team building adheres to the following rules:

items: The opponent cannot bring major legendaries (ex. Mewtwo, Giratina, etc.) unless the player does. Minor legendaries (ex. Kami trio, Manaphy, etc.) can appear any time
Opponents can only bring megas at streak 20+, but Z-Crystals any time
Opponent BST ramps up based on current streak:
0-10: 520 BST max
11-20: 540 BST max
21-30: 570 BST max
31-50: 570 BST max, and duplicate species can be rolled

blocks.html: Wonder Picks

The player can participate in a Wonder Pick feature at the Battle Frontier Pokemon Center. This gives them a Pokemon from the Frontier spreads pool (i.e. the pool opponents, the Battle Factory, and Battle Maze pull from) in exchange for PokeChips. This pool does not include major legendaries. The first pull of the day costs 25 PokeChips, then 50 afterward.
Battle Tower
The Battle Tower provides standard battles with no additional gimmicks and rulesets. It’s the perfect place to enjoy some traditional battles.
Battle Quarry
In this facility, 2 out of 4 move slots are randomly disabled for every Pokemon on the field, both the player and opponent. Moves cannot be reordered while in this facility.
Battle Sands

In the Battle Sands, the same AI that controls Frontier opponents controls the player’s party. The player chooses whether to battle, switch, or forfeit and the AI chooses which move to use. Every Pokemon gets a random stat buff when they enter the field. The intensity of the buff depends on the player’s streak:

items: Streak < 20:  1 stat stage
Streak <40:   2 stat stages
Streak <60:   3 stat stages
Streak <80:   4 stat stages
Streak <100:  5 stat stages

blocks.html: Battle Maze
In this facility, the player is given a random party before every battle, made up of the same Pokemon spread pool the opponent can pull from.
Battle Isle
In this facility, all Pokemon battle with battle behaviours similar to generation 1:

items: Held items are disabled
Abilities are disabled
A move is physical/special based on it’s type (with fairy being special)

blocks.html: The following generation 1 style rules are not applied:

items: Crits are not speed based
Moves do not have a 1/256 chance to miss
Type matchups are not changed

blocks.html: Moves that have dynamic physical/special splits (such as Photon Geyser and Shell Side-Arm) also match their move type every time.
Battle Sim
The Battle Sim applies a random effect to every battle, from the following pool:

rows: Swap random pokemon on each side

blocks.html: The number of effects applied depends on the player’s current streak:

items: Streak < 20:     1 effect
Streak 20-29:   2 effects (doubles only)
Streak 30-39:   2 effects
Streak 40-49:   3 effects
Streak 50-70:   4 effects
Streak 71+:      5 effects

blocks.html: Battle Factory

The Battle Factory tasks the player with renting a party of Pokemon from the same pool an opponent can. After each battle, the player can choose to swap one of their Pokemon with one their opponent just used, with the ability to view the summary of each team before committing.
Battle Observatory

In the battle observatory, the player brings a team of 3 (4 in doubles) Pokemon. The player and opponent reveal their entire teams before choosing 1 (2 in doubles) to duel each other with. The player can view the full summary of their opponent’s team and is encouraged to do so - the AI will read the player’s party to find the best Pokemon to bring in response. In this facility, megas and Z-Crystals are disabled.
